boundaries/2-uEParSheath/gaussianWSinAnd.cause: Bug in the case: the manufactured uEPar carries a factor sin(...)^2 that the sheath condition uEPar = exp(Lambda - phiRef - phi) does not have, so the exact solution does not satisfy the boundary condition and the error is the constant mismatch (about 1.46). With the factor removed the stencil converges at about 4 (2.9e-9, 2.0e-10, 1.3e-11), checked in a Python replica.

boundaries/2-uEParSheath/noYDepInProf.cause: Bug in the case: the manufactured uEPar carries a factor sin(pi x/15)^2 that the sheath condition uEPar = exp(Lambda - phiRef - phi) does not have, so the exact solution does not satisfy the boundary condition and the error is the constant mismatch (about 1.06). With the factor removed the stencil converges at about 4 (2.5e-9, 1.8e-10, 1.2e-11), checked in a Python replica.

boundaries/3-cauchyBC/gaussianWSinAndPar.cause: Bug in the case input: the derivative b is written per unit of y in 0..2pi, but the stencil takes it per unit of coord->dy, which the input sets to Ly/ny (physical length). The two differ by 2pi/Ly, so the ghost value is off by a term that does not shrink with the grid. With b rescaled by 2pi/Ly the error is 4e-9, 4e-10, 7e-11 (order about 3.5 to 4), checked in a Python replica. The warning of the thesis code that the condition is only first order is probably stale. The models do not call this boundary condition, only this case does.

boundaries/3-cauchyBC/noXDepInFunc.cause: Bug in the case input: the derivative b is written per unit of y in 0..2pi, but the stencil takes it per unit of coord->dy, which the input sets to Ly/ny (physical length). The two differ by 2pi/Ly, so the ghost value is off by a term that does not shrink with the grid. Rescaling b by 2pi/Ly gives errors of 1e-9 and falling at order 3.5 to 4 in a Python replica. The models do not call this boundary condition, only this case does.

divOfScalarTimesVector/1a-divPerp/twoGau.cause: Expected property of the scheme, not a bug: Div(f) holds a (1/J) d(J f_x)/dx term; at the first cell next to the axis the 1/J (x = dx/2) multiplies the second-order error of the centred derivative, so the error of that cell falls as dx. Away from the axis (x >= 1) the order is 2, reproduced in a Python replica of the stencil.

divOfScalarTimesVector/2a-divSource/twoG.cause: Bug in the case: the run crashes (segmentation fault) at every resolution. divSource.cxx declares ownOp and never creates it, and div_f_GradPerp_g reads its members J and J2 through that pointer. The probable fix is a call ownOp = OwnOperators::createOperators(); in init(), not tried because it changes guarded C++. The crash is read from the code and the CI log, not reproduced under a debugger. No order is known until it runs.
